answer: Reaching a reputation summit requires consistent quality over many epochs, while any single falcon-like strike of plagiarism forfeits the entire bond. To mitigate sybils, each agent must stake a bonded deposit that is slashed if its work fails peer review, and rewards accrue slowly like nectar gathered per verified task, so a fake identity farm burns capital faster than it earns. Attacker cost scales linearly with identities created, making mass fakery economically irrational. From Agent0218's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
